answer:
Solve the 1D compressible Navier-Stokes equations without heat conduction for the unknowns rho(x,t), v(x,t), and p(x,t) on the domain x in [-1,1] and t in [0,0.5].
Use Gamma = 1.6666666666666667, eta = 0.1, and zeta = eta = 0.1.
Use the conservative variables U = [rho, m, E] with m = rho*v and E = p/(Gamma-1) + 0.5*rho*v^2.
Evolve the conservative PDE system rho_t + (m)_x = 0, m_t + (m^2/rho + p - sigma)_x = 0, and E_t + ((E+p)*v - v*sigma)_x = 0, where sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x.
Use a uniform finite-volume grid with Nx = 400 cells on [-1,1], so dx = 2/400 = 0.005.
Place cell centers at x_j = -1 + (j+0.5)*dx for j = 0,...,399.
Set initial conditions pointwise at cell centers using rho(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*sin(pi*x), v(x,0) = 0.1*cos(pi*x), and p(x,0) = 1.0 + 0.2*cos(pi*x).
Use radians for all trigonometric functions.
Reconstruct pressure using the equation of state p = (Gamma-1)*(E - 0.5*m^2/rho), and clip rho and p to a small floor of 1e-12 if needed to enforce positivity.
Use the Rusanov local Lax-Friedrichs numerical flux for the inviscid Euler part with F_conv(U) = [m, m^2/rho + p, (E+p)*v] and v = m/rho.
Compute the interface wave speed as a = max(|v_L| + c_L, |v_R| + c_R) with c = sqrt(Gamma*p/rho).
Compute the convective numerical flux as F_hat = 0.5*(F_conv(U_L) + F_conv(U_R)) - 0.5*a*(U_R - U_L).
Compute v_x at cell centers using centered differences of the cell-centered v values.
Compute sigma = (zeta + 4/3*eta)*v_x at cell centers and approximate sigma at interfaces by averaging neighboring cell-centered sigma values.
Add the viscous interface flux F_visc = [0, -sigma, -v*sigma] using interface-averaged v and sigma.
Use the total interface flux F_total = F_hat + F_visc.
Integrate in time using the 2-stage SSP-RK2 Heun method on the semi-discrete finite-volume system.
Use CFL = 0.4.
Choose the time step each step as dt_conv = CFL*dx / max_j(|v_j| + c_j), dt_visc = 0.5*dx^2 / max(zeta + 4/3*eta, 1e-30), and dt = min(dt_conv, dt_visc).
Adjust the final time step so the final time T = 0.5 is hit exactly.
Implement periodic boundary conditions by wrapping ghost cell indices to the opposite side of the domain.
At T = 0.5, compute rho(x,T), v(x,T), and p(x,T) on the cell centers.
Save the file "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.npz" containing arrays x, rho, v, p and scalars Gamma, eta, zeta, T, dx, and CFL.
Save a three-panel line plot of rho, v, and p versus x at time T as "solution_pdebench_cns1d_eta0p1_periodic_smooth.png".
Print the minimum and maximum of rho and p as a positivity check, and print the mean of rho over the domain as a mass conservation check.
Use Python exponentiation with ** for powers when writing code.
